text: Every cited source was actually opened by the researcher during the task.

For the task "Build a small HTTP JSON API, using only the Python standard library (no third-party dependencies), for consulting a mock database of books. Endpoints: list all books, get one book by id (return 404 if": The sources/ directory is empty, so there are no reference files. I read the official Python http.server documentation, which confirms the API can be built with the standard library alone. The route and schema suggestions at the end are my recommendations, not facts from a source.

For the task "Build a small HTTP JSON API, using only the Python standard library (no third-party dependencies), for consulting a mock database of books. Endpoints: list all books, get one book by id (return 404 if": sources/ is empty, so there are no reference files. I read the official Python http.server documentation (opened at https://docs.python.org/3/library/http.server.html). It confirms the API can be built with the standard library alone. The design suggestions below (routes, JSON shape, test approach) are my recommendations, not facts from a source.

The design is sufficient to meet every requirement's acceptance criterion, and interfaces between work items are precise enough to build them separately. Auditor's advice last time: Make the allowlist one precise, shared constant in the design. Either add ast, os (or pathlib), contextlib and io to the "Imports allowed" list and say the W1 ast test must use exactly that list plus {bookapi, tests}, or say the test checks against sys.stdlib_module_names on 3.10+ and an explicit fallback set otherwise. Also say W2 must not import modules outside that list.
